review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent planning expectation for the frozen C bundle. Repository identity/base commit, REQ/AC keys, exact writable binding scopes, task keys, eligible agents, readiness and evidence stages agree with the original specification. C explicitly fixes OPT-1 as a hypothetical input without asserting a human Decision; its empty decision-input fingerprint is therefore consistent. This does not resolve the paired B scenario: a material unresolved DEC-001 must still block B at decisions. The source evidence supports the bounded owner set: message formatting belongs in HTTPError, option declarations and normalization in options/Ky, and fetch filtering in constants. Existing generic forwarding, merging and hook declaration consumers appropriately remain inspection owners. The supplied build configuration supports generated distribution declarations rather than separately maintained declaration owners, and tsconfig.test.json includes the proposed test-d file for compile-time validation. The implementation and dependent independent-verification expectations are supported by the supplied project-scoped active capability claims, role membership and availability; the configured independent reviewer satisfies the stated non-executing review prerequisite. Pending legacy claims and persona descriptions are not needed as eligibility evidence. Source fingerprint differences are explained by the manifest/evaluation digest domains and PRD trim-only persistence. Gold and preview release fingerprints agree across repository, source, team, decision, prompt, model, sampling, budgets and metric policy. Historical project reuse and retained old operations do not constitute candidate evidence for this bundle under the supplied isolation facts. This approval relies on the supplied Service-bound fingerprints and provenance; I did not recompute digests, execute code, verify test outcomes or provide human attestation.
